name: Ory
abstract: Open-source (Apache 2.0) microservice-based CIAM platform. Modular architecture: Ory Kratos (identity), Ory Hydra (OAuth2/OIDC, OpenID Certified), Ory Keto (Zanzibar-based FGA permissions), Ory Oathkeeper (Zero Trust proxy). Unique aDAU pricing model.

features.description: Unlimited social connections on all tiers. Native Sign in with Google and Apple on iOS/Android.
WebAuthn/FIDO2 passkeys on all tiers including free.
Passwordless magic code (email OTP) for sign-up and login.
Passwordless SMS code.
Passwordless magic code via email (email OTP). Classic magic links supported.
Ory Kratos does not support anonymous or guest authentication sessions. All sessions require an identity with registered credentials or external OIDC provider.
TOTP authenticator app MFA on all tiers including free.
Ory Kratos supports TOTP (RFC 6238) and WebAuthn for second-factor authentication, but does not support HMAC-based counter OTP (HOTP, RFC 4226).
WebAuthn hardware security keys for U2F MFA.
Ory does not offer native mobile push notification MFA or a proprietary mobile authenticator application.
Ory does not provide built-in risk-based or adaptive MFA. MFA requirements are configured statically per flow or managed programmatically via webhooks.
Ory does not include a native Cisco Duo MFA integration. External second-factor providers can be integrated via webhooks.
Enforce aal2 (second factor) for specific operations via the ?aal=aal2 query parameter on the login endpoint.
Ory Hydra is OpenID Certified.
SAML SSO via BoxyHQ acquisition (May 2025). Enterprise tier or Enterprise License. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
Ory implements modern OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 standards. Legacy WS-Federation protocol is not supported.
OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant via Ory Hydra. Billed per token.
OIDC-based B2B SSO available on Growth tier+. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
SAML enterprise SSO available on Enterprise tier. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
Ory Kratos does not support direct LDAP/Active Directory synchronization. Enterprise federation with Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory is supported via OIDC/SAML in Ory Network.
Microsoft Entra ID via OIDC social login provider.
Bulk user import supported on all tiers.
Import password hashes. Password migration hook for lazy migration when hashes unavailable.
The Ory Kratos identity import API returns 409 Conflict when attempting to import an identity that already exists. Bulk upsert is not supported in a single import operation.
Ory Kratos enforces JSON Schema validation on all imported identities, requiring traits to conform strictly to configured identity schemas.
The Ory Kratos identity import endpoint only supports importing password credentials and OIDC social links. Pre-enrolled TOTP secrets or WebAuthn credentials cannot be imported.
SCIM 2.0 provisioning via Ory Polis (BoxyHQ). Enterprise tier or Enterprise License. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
SCIM 2.0 outbound provisioning via Ory Polis. Enterprise tier. Launched April 2025.
SCIM group sync via Ory Polis. Enterprise tier. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
Users are created on first social/enterprise SSO login.
Zero-downtime migrations on all tiers. Password migration hook for lazy migration.
Ory Account Experience self-service pages. Ory Elements component library.
Automatic account linking for social + password accounts sharing the same email.
Deactivate identities via Admin API.
Custom profile fields via JSON Schema-based Ory Identity Schemas.
Metadata traits and public/admin metadata on identities.

Ory Kratos stores identity traits and metadata as JSON objects in the underlying database without arbitrary application-layer limits; size limits are constrained by SQL database column types and JSON Schema rules.
Via Ory Keto Zanzibar-based permission system. Permission checks billed per-use.
B2B Organizations via Ory Polis. Multi-tenant production environments require Enterprise tier on Ory Network. Self-hosted (Open Source) has no restrictions.
Username format rules via JSON Schema identity schema.
Progressive profiling can be built using Ory Kratos identity schemas and custom registration/settings UI flows, but Ory does not provide a visual drag-and-drop progressive form builder.
Ory Keto supports relationship-based checks that model ABAC patterns.
Ory Keto implements Google Zanzibar. FGA available on all paid tiers.
OAuth 2.0 scopes and audience restrictions via Ory Hydra.
Ory Network does not currently offer standard HIPAA Business Associate Agreements (BAAs). For self-hosted Ory deployments, compliance is managed by the customer.
Ory Network certifications focus on SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; a standalone PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance (AoC) is not provided.
Ory does not publish a CSA STAR certification. Ory maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications.
Ory Network does not hold FedRAMP authorization. Self-hosted Ory open-source instances can be operated within customer FedRAMP environments.
GDPR-friendly storage with data locality built-in.
OAuth 2.0 consent flows via Ory Hydra. GDPR-friendly consent management.
PII region storage selection on all paid tiers. Migrate PII storage regions supported. Self-hosted (Open Source) can deploy in any region.
Self-hosted or Ory Enterprise License for dedicated deployment on AWS or Azure.
Customer activity insights with historical depth varying by tier.
Live event streaming and event firehose to data lake on Enterprise tier. Self-hosted has no restrictions.
Ory Network uses Cloudflare WAF and edge security, but does not provide a tenant-configurable SIEM or threat monitoring security dashboard.
Self-hosted deployment allows full key management.
Fully managed CAPTCHA on all tiers.
Credential stuffing and brute force protection on all tiers.
Suspicious IP throttling on all tiers.
Breached password detection on all tiers including free.
Ory does not provide built-in dark web monitoring for compromised credentials. Password policies and hashing algorithms (Argon2id, bcrypt) are enforced locally.
Ory Network does not expose customer-configurable IP access control lists (ACLs) in the console. IP restrictions must be enforced at the application or edge reverse proxy level.
Ory does not offer native device fingerprinting or client risk profiling. Active sessions track IP address, user-agent, and authentication timestamps.
Multi-brand projects and themeable self-service pages.
In Ory Network, MFA policies are defined at the project level. Per-organization MFA policy enforcement in B2B scenarios requires project segregation or custom webhook checks.
No-code self-service pages (hosted login, registration, recovery, settings).
Headless API-first architecture. Bring Your Own UI with full flow control. Ory Elements (React/Preact/Next.js).
No Ory branding required. Headless architecture means full brand control.
Multi-language (i18n) with built-in translations for multiple languages.
Ory Elements: React, Preact, Next.js component library. Plus no-code self-service pages.
Live analytics on all paid tiers. Historical analytics: 7 days (Production), 30 days (Growth), 90 days (Enterprise).
SDKs for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, PHP, Rust, .NET, Java, and more.
Per-plan rate limits documented: Developer 5 rps burst/150 rpm; Production 40 rps burst/900 rpm.
Actions/webhooks for auth flow customization. Ory Oathkeeper for Zero Trust proxy with mutation rules.
Webhook endpoints and Bring Your Own UI are language-agnostic, including TypeScript.
1 custom domain per project on Production/Growth, custom count on Enterprise.
Ory CLI for automation, configuration management, and CI/CD.
Ory Kratos uses its own DB. Password migration hooks enable connecting to external DBs for lazy migration.
Actions and webhooks for auth events on all tiers. Live event streaming on Enterprise.
Fully customizable self-service pages and custom email templates.
Custom SMTP via Ory's courier system.
Custom claims via token hooks and Ory Hydra token enrichment.
No-code self-service pages via Ory Network console. Not a visual drag-and-drop flow builder.
Ory does not provide built-in identity document verification or biometric liveness checks. Integration with identity verification providers is handled via webhook hooks.
OAuth2 Verifiable Credentials support via Ory Hydra.
Ory is a dedicated identity and authorization infrastructure platform with no built-in billing, subscription tiering, or payment gateway integration.
Ory positions for agentic AI identity. OAuth2 M2M via Ory Hydra for agent authentication.

Ory Kratos/Hydra are written in Go and can serve TLS natively, though Ory's own production docs recommend terminating TLS at a gateway/load balancer instead. While Go 1.24 (Feb 2025) enables X25519MLKEM768 in crypto/tls by default when native TLS is used, no Ory-specific statement or documentation confirms PQC TLS support. Without vendor evidence, status is unknown.
Ory Hydra signs tokens using standard RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA cryptographic algorithms. Post-quantum signature algorithms (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) are not supported.

No public roadmap, blog post, whitepaper, or GitHub discussion found describing PQC migration plans for Ory. Ory's public security page and trust center make no mention of post-quantum or quantum-safe cryptography.
Ory does not support post-quantum encryption algorithms or HPKE (RFC 9180) for JWE token or credential encryption.
Ory Hydra supports mTLS client authentication using standard X.509 RSA/ECDSA certificates. Post-quantum or hybrid certificates are not supported.
Ory does not support NIST SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signature schemes (LMS/HSS, XMSS).
